message.content:
**Top Five Flower Species for Pollination in South America**

| Rank | Flower Species (Common & Scientific Name) | Key Pollinators | Why It’s Important |
|------|-------------------------------------------|-----------------|--------------------|
| 1 | **Heliconia spp.** (Hummingbird‑heliconia) | Hummingbirds, bees | Bright, nectar‑rich bracts attract hummingbirds; also visited by bees and butterflies. |
| 2 | **Erythrina spp.** (Coral tree) | Bees, bats, birds | Produces large, showy flowers with abundant pollen; important for both diurnal and nocturnal pollinators. |
| 3 | **Cattleya spp.** (Orchid) | Bees, moths, butterflies | Orchid’s complex structure offers specialized pollination mechanisms; many species are endemic to the Amazon. |
| 4 | **Passiflora spp.** (Passionflower) | Bees, hummingbirds, bats | Diverse floral morphology supports a wide range of pollinators; crucial for seed dispersal. |
| 5 | **Spathiphyllum spp.** (Peace lily) | Bees, flies | Though often cultivated, native species play a role in forest understory pollination networks. |

These species are among the most ecologically significant for pollination across diverse South American habitats—from tropical rainforests to Andean cloud forests—due to their high nectar production, attractive floral displays, and specialized relationships with local pollinators.
